A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable text, equations, figures, and complete appendices. V1 Appendices A–F correspond to v2 Appendices B–G; v2 adds a related-work appendix.

before.justification: Section 6 and Figure 2 report original synthetic experiments comparing attention approximation errors against Wanda and SparseGPT.

after.justification: V2 retains the synthetic results and adds original C4/Llama 3.2-1B attention experiments, assumption checks, and end-to-end perplexity results in Sections 6.2–6.3.

M1.justification: Although Algorithm 1 is retained, v2 introduces a substantial adaptation for real models: Equation (1) optimizes separate query and key masks, M_Q and M_K, with separate penalties. V1 optimizes one mask on the fused matrix W_Q W_K^T. This changes the optimization variables and weights being pruned.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates synthetic Gaussian inputs and constructed weight matrices. V2 retains that coverage and adds C4 data with pretrained Llama 3.2-1B, covering both attention reconstruction and downstream language-model perplexity.

E2.justification: Wanda and SparseGPT remain the pruning comparators. The new perplexity comparison additionally includes an explicit fully dense model reference and evaluates attention-pruning comparisons within dense, Wanda-pruned, and SparseGPT-pruned MLP configurations.

E3.justification: The synthetic protocol is retained. V2 adds last-attention-layer evaluation with d = 2048 and an end-to-end protocol using eight C4 training sentences for calibration and 128 validation sentences for perplexity. It also introduces 50% pruning settings and controlled comparisons across three MLP configurations.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained synthetic sensitivity analysis, v2 adds real-model sequence-length and sparsity sweeps in Figure 3, reports checks of the theoretical assumptions with beta approximately 0.034 and delta approximately 0.0025, and tests compatibility with different MLP-pruning choices in Table 1.

E5.justification: Figure 2 retains the same shaded bands without an explanation of their statistical meaning. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, and v2 introduces no confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 2's synthetic results are retained. V2 adds real-model attention-error curves and perplexity results. With a dense MLP, Table 1 reports 13.885 for the proposed method, 14.269 for SparseGPT, 14.912 for Wanda, and 12.487 for the fully dense model. These are new-setting results, not improvements to previously reported scores.

T1.justification: The main theorems and matched proof appendices retain their mathematical content. V2 corrects Remark 4.2's pruned-attention expression by replacing W with M ◦ W and introduces the two-mask objective in Equation (1). It supplies no corresponding extension of the convergence proof.

C1.justification: The nonlinear-pruning novelty and convergence contributions remain central. V2 strengthens the main empirical positioning by explicitly claiming superiority over Wanda and SparseGPT in the abstract and contributions, and extends that claim to real C4/Llama evaluations in the introduction.

C2.justification: V2 adds an interpretation of attention pruning as compatible with existing linear MLP-pruning methods, using Table 1 to argue broader practical applicability. It also presents the numerical assumption checks as validation of the theoretical framework. The earlier synthetic-result explanations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds hidden-state extraction through a customized hook, calibration and evaluation sample counts, and real-model hyperparameters. Documentation remains inconsistent: Equation (1) omits the stated regularization coefficient, while Figure 3's right panel labels lambda as 0.005 despite the setup specifying 0.05.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially broadens literature coverage to foundation models, adaptation, prompting, reasoning, and additional efficiency research. V2 also adds citations supporting the C4/Llama experiments. These additions go beyond bibliographic updates to retained works; the original pruning and attention-acceleration positioning remains.

P1.justification: V2 makes grammatical edits, converts several numbered subsections into paragraph headings, consolidates the earlier experimental settings and results under synthetic evaluation, and adds separate real-model subsections. The main narrative and matched proof text remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the empirical displays with a two-panel real-model comparison in Figure 3 and the grouped perplexity comparison in Table 1. Figures 1 and 2 retain their content; Figure 2 is relocated, and several displayed equations are compacted into inline text.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's synthetic-only evidence, the C4/Llama experiments and controlled perplexity comparisons provide useful practical validation. However, the evaluated two-mask variant is not covered by the unchanged convergence proof, and conflicting regularization specifications hinder reproducibility. The empirical relevance improves, but these gaps limit support for the strengthened claims.
